subject: Opscale renewal: restructuring term + incremental capacity buckets
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia@opscale.com>, Derek Huang <derek@opscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning — flexible structure proposal

Hi Alicia / Derek,

Per our Q4 check-in, Opscale's current term ends 2027-01-01 and you flagged wanting more predictable unit economics while keeping room to scale. To balance those goals we drafted a different structure I wanted to run by you before legal/finance get involved: 

- Primary term: 24 months (2027-01-01 -> 2028-12-31) to avoid mid-year true-ups
- Incremental capacity buckets: three pre-priced add-on pools (Q1 ramp, Q2 expansion, tail reserve) you can draw from monthly
- Frontloaded credits: modest one-time credit to offset transition friction if you commit to a 24-mo term
- Auto-renew: off by default; renewal conversation kicks 90 days prior to term end

If this sounds directionally right, I can loop in Ben with an updated pricing workbook and Kim for SOW redline.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Quick sync (20m) this week to confirm bucket sizes / expected draw patterns
2) Draft SOW with incremental-bucket pricing and simple co-terming language

Thanks — happy to adjust.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Ramos <alicia@opscale.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@opscale.com
Date: 2026-10-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — flexible structure proposal

Thanks Hannah — this is helpful context. A couple of notes from our side: 

- We like the idea of pre-priced buckets but need a clearer mechanism so we don't overpay in early months. Can you show a stepped rate (lower unit price once we hit tier thresholds)?
- Would prefer an 18- or 24-month term that co-terms to our fiscal year (we run to Dec 31) — sounds like your 24-mo suggestion lines up
- Procurement will want a simple auto-renew opt-in (we prefer explicit renewal rather than automatic)

One request: our finance team needs a front-loaded credit to cover migration spike in Q1 (target ~$35k). Is that something Redwood can do as a one-time credit against the first invoice?

Cc'ing procurement so they have context. Happy to join a 20m call if it helps.

—Alicia
Alicia Ramos
Head of Cloud Ops, Opscale

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — credit & stepped rates idea + pricing workbook attached

Hannah / Marcus — building on Alicia's asks. I put together a pricing sheet that has: 
- Baseline 24-mo commitment tier 
- Three incremental buckets (25k, 75k, 200k tokens/month equivalents) with stepped unit discounts at each threshold
- One-time migration credit: $35,000 applied to first invoice (we can increase to $40k if we need to sweeten)

I've attached "pricing-incremental-buckets.xlsx" with a few scenarios (50/25/25 split vs. frontloaded 60/20/20). The stepped pricing ensures Opscale's marginal cost drops as they consume more; that addresses the "don't overpay early" concern.

If Marcus and legal are good with the mechanics, we can ship a redlined SOW next week.

Cheers,
Ben
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference
Attachment: pricing-incremental-buckets.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: SOW language + co-term mechanics (draft)

Kim / Hannah — I reviewed Ben's pricing workbook. Key legal points I recommend we include in the SOW: 

1) Definition of incremental buckets and draw-down process (monthly invoiced draws, unused capacity expires at quarter end unless rolled per written request)
2) True-up window: 30 days after quarter close for reconciliation
3) Frontloaded credit: one-time credit applied to first invoice; non-refundable, non-transferable
4) Co-term language: primary term ends 2028-12-31; any partial months prorated; no automatic permanent price lock — discounts apply only to specified buckets

I've attached a short redline I can fold into the SOW. Also flagging that SOC 2 artifacts may be requested; Hannah, please share the standard evidence bundle so procurement has what they need.

-Marcus
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Opscale_SOW_v2_redline.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia@opscale.com>, procurement@opscale.com
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T10:20:00-08:00
Subject: Opscale SOW & SOC2 evidence

Hi Alicia / procurement team,

Attached is our redlined SOW (Opscale_SOW_v2_redline.pdf) and a short SOC 2 evidence bundle (SOC2-evidence-summary.zip). The SOW implements the incremental-bucket model we discussed and includes the $35k migration credit applied to the first invoice.

Key callouts for your review: 
- Term: 24 months co-terming to calendar year (2027-01-01 -> 2028-12-31)
- Buckets: three pre-priced pools, monthly invoicing and 30-day true-up
- Auto-renew: set to "off"; we will issue a renewal reminder 90 days prior

Please route any legal comments to me (cc Hannah) and procurement for commercial/PO questions. If everything looks good we can route to DocuSign.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Opscale_SOW_v2_redline.pdf, SOC2-evidence-summary.zip

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia@opscale.com>, procurement@opscale.com, Derek Huang <derek@opscale.com>

Date: 2026-11-30T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Finalized structure & signature link — next steps

Alicia / Derek / Procurement — thank you for the review and constructive back-and-forth. Per the attached/redlined SOW and pricing workbook, here is the agreed structure we will put into DocuSign: 

- Term: 24 months, co-term to calendar year (2027-01-01 through 2028-12-31)
- Incremental capacity buckets: three pre-priced add-on pools (Q1 ramp / Q2 expansion / tail reserve) with stepped unit discounts at thresholds listed in the pricing sheet
- Migration credit: $35,000 applied to the first invoice
- Auto-renew: disabled; renewal conversation triggered 90 days prior to term end
- True-up: 30 days after each quarter close; unused bucket capacity expires at quarter end unless Opscale requests roll-forward in writing

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/link/OP-2026-5543-sign
Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/opsale/OP-2026-5543/pricing-sheet

Next steps for Opscale: 
1) Confirm final SOW acceptance by signing via DocuSign (link above)
2) Send PO reference to procurement@redwood.ai once signed
3) Marissa will schedule a 30m onboarding + billing cadence call for the first week of January

If you want a short call to walk Ops through the bucket draw-down mechanics I can set something up this week. Thanks again — looking forward to continuing to scale with Opscale.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing-incremental-buckets.xlsx
